result.description: Ecommerce-focused customer support helpdesk (tickets, customers, macros, integrations) with a REST API.
result.auth_detail: Private apps: HTTP Basic with account email + API key (key created in Settings > REST API). Public apps: OAuth2 auth-code (client_id/secret from partner account; 24h access token, non-expiring refresh token; scopes). Per-account subdomain base URL.
result.access_detail: API key is self-serve for a Gorgias account admin (7-day free trial, no card). But a multi-tenant OAuth2 public app must be approved by Gorgias before it appears in the helpdesk app list. API plan restriction not confirmed on the pricing page.
result.api_notes: REST API at https://{subdomain}.gorgias.com/api with OAuth2 scopes (customers, tickets, integrations, etc.). The scope list suggests core helpdesk objects are covered. I did not fetch the full endpoint list, so breadth is inferred.
result.blocker: Public OAuth2 app needs Gorgias approval. Until then, use per-account API key (Basic auth). Vendor MCP claim comes from search snippets (Merge and Ringly), not from Gorgias docs, which returned 404.

evidence.quote: Please remember that the API key authentication method can be used only for private apps.
If you plan to build a public app you have to use OAuth2.
In order to be able to have an approved public app with Gorgias, it is required that the app is using OAuth2 for authentication.
As an admin, you can easily generate and revoke your access token in the settings of your account.
OAuth2 scopes allow to limit your app's access to Gorgias user’s account data.
